headline: Harry Kane wins Ballon d'Or, first English winner in 25 years, beating Yamal & Mbappe
summary: Harry Kane, 33, scored 73 goals in 65 games last season, propelling Bayern Munich to a double. Alexia Putellas claimed her third women's Ballon d'Or, extending Spain's domination.
details: Harry Kane became England's first Ballon d'Or winner in 25 years in his native city of London on Monday, beating out stiff competition from Lamine Yamal and Kylian Mbappe. This marks the crowning glory of his career to date.

The 33-year-old Bayern Munich forward struck a remarkable 73 goals in 65 games for club and country last season. He propelled the German giants to a league and cup double and also scored six times as England finished third at the World Cup.

Kane expressed his gratitude to his Bayern Munich team-mates, stating that their push and competition made the achievement possible. His medal collection was previously limited to German domestic triumphs since his arrival at Bayern in 2023.

Alexia Putellas claimed the women's prize for a third time, extending Spain's domination of the award. Her role in leading Barcelona to last season's Champions League before moving to London City Lionesses was a key factor.

Putellas's third Ballon d'Or caps her return to the top of the women's game after an anterior cruciate ligament injury derailed her rise four years ago. She succeeds Spain team-mate Aitana Bonmati, the winner for the past three years, who was sidelined by a leg break for most of last season.

Other notable awards included Luis de la Fuente being named men's coach of the year after leading Spain to World Cup glory, and Barcelona's Pere Romeu scooping the prize for women's coach of the year. Arsenal's Bukayo Saka won the Socrates award for his humanitarian work.

Paris Saint-Germain, despite winning a second consecutive Champions League, missed out on any of the main individual awards but received the consolation of men's club of the year. Spanish duo Unai Simon and Cata Coll were named best men's and women's goalkeepers respectively.

headline_marked: [[Alexia Putellas wins Ballon d'Or Feminin award]] for outstanding season
headline: Alexia Putellas wins Ballon d'Or Feminin award for outstanding season
summary: Spain midfielder Alexia Putellas was presented with the highest individual honour in women's football on Monday, following another season of success for both her club and country.
details: Spain midfielder Alexia Putellas was presented with the Ballon d'Or Feminin award on Monday, receiving the highest individual honour in women's football. This recognition follows her exceptional performance over the past year for both club and country.

An international panel of journalists selected Putellas as the standout performer. She notably won the treble with Barcelona in the 2025-26 campaign before her move to Women's Super League side London City Lionesses in July.
